plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no additional information about the other bidders' distributions beyond uniform draws, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This is because I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win with a bid above value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $47, I will bid $47 to ensure optimal outcomes.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks negative profit and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $41, I should bid exactly $41 to maximize expected profit.
